Break it into thirds by effort, not by stopping. Start the first third truly easy, where you could chat in full sentences, settle into steady for the middle, and keep the last third controlled rather than fast. The most common mistake is going out too quick and paying for it late.

For the long run itself, a few things help. Take water or fuel on a schedule instead of waiting until you're thirsty or flat, roughly every 20 to 30 minutes on longer efforts. Or split it by landmarks, like three loops or three out-and-backs, so the mileage feels like three short runs.

If walk breaks appeal to you, a minute of walking every 10 minutes or so is a legitimate strategy, not a failure. It keeps the effort even and often lets people go farther.

How long is your long run right now? I can tell you more once I know the distance, or I can build the run into your plan if you want it set up.
